utterances.text: Training/briefings on how the forms were going to be used, how to -- procedures to ensure that women were involved if statements were being taken by -- from women, particularly of a sexual, violent-type nature. So these were briefings on managing people in distress, recognising that they have other critical issues going on in refugee camps. So these were more briefings/trainings to acclimate people to work in that type of a very stressful environment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does that mean that those people had no similar experience prior to this training?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have similar experience. I mean, a lot of these people were police officers, et cetera, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why was it necessary for them to receive such training since you said they had previous experiences, that they were police officers, that they were they were the creme de la creme? Why would they require additional training? Could you please explain that to me.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've answered that, Your Honour. But these were -- Whether you call it a training, a briefing, it was on the management of the information that was being collected, it was how to conduct interviewing if children are there, if women are present, how to manage the stress, how to watch out for your interpreter, these types of things that needed to be re-emphasised in this kind of critical humanitarian situation, which isn't usually covered in normal police training courses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have I correctly noted yesterday that when you were actually in Kosovo of the monitoring force, only 75 were human rights officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 75 were assigned to our department, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that we're now talking about 200?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you were taking in people who hadn't the human rights working experience in Kosovo that some of your team had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a bit of an administrative issue, to be honest. I had 75 people in my department, but there was also other verifiers managing police issues, military issues, that would have the same types of skills and be doing the same types of activities but not necessarily in my division, and then we brought them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is precisely what I wanted to have clarified. The witness said that the mission was down-sized to 200; whereas instead it was actually increased from 75 to 200 and that there was additional training conducted. In that regard I have a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were there any local members of staff among the people trained in the mission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I would beg to interfere to just respectfully suggest that a question taken from a cross-examination statement is very rarely used for another question of cross-examination unless there is something really to clarify. And I'm seeing that some of the questions are being taken from answers to questions raised in cross-examination. This would only retract the matter without much help. I would request that this may kindly be avoided. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please provide an answer to this question: Among the people who were additionally trained, were there any locals?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. But you also inaccurately stated a conclusion in your question, which was I said the mission shrunk from 1300 to 450. The human rights division did, in fact, expand. Yes, we had local staff working with us in the camps in Albania and in Macedonia. Where possible, these were people that were also working with the KVM inside Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the local personnel also took statements from refugees?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local personnel were working with the internationals in the translation, so they were part of the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you recall on what date after your withdrawal from Kosovo you arrived in Albania and on what date you arrived in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the mission withdrew on March 20th, and that was directly to Skopje. It was then, I think, early April, the 3rd or 4th, when the OSCE Permanent Council took a decision to boost the capacity of the mission in Albania because of the huge humanitarian crisis that was being created in the north with 45.000-plus refugees a day crossing for a three- or four-day period. And I believe all of that was around April 3rd, 4th, 5th, something, and that was about the time that we then deployed to Albania and in -- within two or three days had set up in all 12 prefectures, municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Once you arrived in Macedonia and Albania, had the refugee camps already been set up?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When were they set up?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Stenkovic 1 and 2 in Skopje were set up probably starting around the 28th or 29th of March, a week or two after we got there, and they were being set up as people were coming over. Both countries were reacting to the in-flow. But in Macedonia many people stayed with host families, so that the camps came on line -- I think it was the end of March or early April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you talk about setting up in all 12 municipalities, that's Albanian -- municipalities in Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how many municipalities are there in Albania in total?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they call them prefectures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From your testimony we heard that your people conducted interviews with over -- or rather, with several thousand refugees. Do you have the data on any of the refugees perhaps stating that they went to Macedonia or Albania because of NATO bombings?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some statements to that effect, but the overwhelming majority were -- the reason was because of the forced expulsion by Serbian army and security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Mitchell, if I were to tell you that I have information that, for example, Pristina itself was bombed on 406 occasions, Prizren 362, Djakovica, 268, Urosevac 266 times, doesn't it seem illogical that but a few refugees confirmed that they actually fled the bombings and the number of those people is insignificant?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it's very consistent. People leave because they're forced to leave. If there's bombing, usually people hunker down in their basements. But getting people out of their house at the scale of more than 1 million is done with force and with the end of a gun, and in this situation it was the Serbian police and army and security forces that expelled the people from Kosovo. And that is what they told us and that's what's in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I believe that the answer speaks for itself, and my last question to you will be this. Did you find any shelters around Kosovo, shelters against air-raids in villages, since you're saying that in such cases people actually find shelter?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing any bomb shelters. Usually people said they went to the basements of their houses or the basements of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And those basements were enough to protect them from bombing. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will have some questions for cross-examination of this witness. If I could just get the podium for a second to organise myself and hopefully go through these in an efficient manner. I apologise, Your Honour. It looks like the equipment doesn't fit on the newly revised desk, so I'll have to make do with this method.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Ivetic, and along with my colleague Mr. Branko Lukic I'm one of the attorneys representing Sreten Lukic in these proceedings, and I hope to ask you a series of questions this afternoon, and I will try not to unduly repeat topics that have been previously exhausted by my colleagues. But one thing at the get-go that I guess I have to ask is that I believe I'm reading here in the transcript that you just responded to my colleague, Mr. Bakrac, saying that something in the area of more than 1 million people were expelled by force from Kosovo and Metohija and that that force was by the Serbian police and the Serbian military and that that is what they told us. Are you now implying that over 1 million people in Albania and Macedonia were interviewed by your mission?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. But the sampling that we interviewed of 2 and a half thousand all had the exact same story, and we were hearing it from others, whose statements we were unable to collect for -- because of the sheer volume.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are you claiming that there were 1 million persons displaced outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: More than a million, actually, is I think what you said.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of Kosovo I think the reliable numbers are the UNHCR numbers which I think are around 850.000, with estimations of internal displacement of another 4 or 500.000. That's how that number is compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, ma'am, you indicated that all the statements that you received from these people were identical. Isn't that in direct contradiction to what you said a few minutes earlier that you did have statements that people left due to NATO bombings?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe my answer was that the overwhelming number of statements indicated that the reason was not because of the NATO bombing. And I did acknowledge that there were some statements to the effect that NATO was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I direct you to page 50, line 14, 15, and 16 of your testimony, ma'am. You did not say that. You said: "All had the exact same story." So are you perhaps embellishing the facts somewhat?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you stand by your statement that all had the same story?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by the statement that all of the people that we interviewed, the overwhelming number of them said they left because of the conduct of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll get to some questions about how you selected people to interview. But, first of all, I want to ask you some other questions relating to the methodology that was utilised by your staff in order to obtain the information for your report, the -- and when I say "your report," I'm referring to the Kosovo/Kosova As Seen, As Told. So please, when I use the term "report," unless I state otherwise, that's what I'm referring to. Based upon the mission and goal of your staff at the time, wouldn't it be fair to say that the purpose of this report was essentially to do work for the Office of the Prosecutor here at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is to say, rather than being merely a collector of facts, the objective of the report was not only to collect facts but to make and reach legal conclusions and present legal arguments that crimes had been committed and to argue that perpetrators of those crimes should be brought to trial?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the purpose of all human rights reporting, including this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But I submit, ma'am, that the method in which you -- you used the term "sample group," did you not, the sample that you selected for interviews in the various camps?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the manner in which the sample group was collected, first of all, isn't it accurate that this sample group consisted of only 2.764 refugees?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the -- that sounds like the exact number, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Because we've heard various numbers thrown around and I'm trying to pin that down.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the report in front of me, but if it says it in that, then that sounds about right. I usually say 2800.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And these interviews were all conducted at the refugee centres that you have described for us in Macedonia and Albania?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some -- yeah, some were collected in the camps. Others were collected from people that may have been in housed families in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And from these 2.764 people that were interviewed, your staff extrapolated from those results to reach conclusions and inferences based upon the refugee population as a whole. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusions and inferences are of the situation, the human rights situation, that was unfolding -- I find your question a little bit confusing. Do you mind asking it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sure. The -- the responses you received from these 2.764 individuals which are contained in your report, the OSCE report, from that, the report, which was completed by your staff, extrapolates and draws conclusions relating to the entire refugee population, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It draws conclusions related to the entire human rights situation that was going on, yes, and the causes for that displacement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, in your testimony a few moments ago did you not in fact extrapolate and make conclusions based upon what you knew these 2.764 individuals had said and relate it to the entire refugee population?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just -- it was more than that. It was also the follow-up work and the verification when we went back into Kosovo. So yes, with that caveat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we had heard that during the interviews they were either conducted in these orange OSCE trucks or in tents that were visibly identified as being the OSCE, conspicuous to the public and to other people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe your staff found people to interview based upon asking to speak only to victims of crimes. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was more that people flooded us and then with -- wanting to give statements and we prioritised who we would take those statements from. We were looking for victims and direct witness accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, isn't it true that your report actually states that rather than randomly asking people, your staff turned to Kosovo Albanian leaders in the refugee centres, such as family patriarchs and imams, to find people for you to interview?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it was more to help filter as opposed to find, because we were getting so many requests that we were relying on contacts, as you've described, to help us find the best statements, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you used these people to help you select the best statements?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The best statements to prove the OTP's case here. Is that not accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best statements to describe what the events were in Kosovo and what -- from people that were best able to articulate it. That's what we were striving to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact is it fair to say that on occasion these people interviewed consisted of multiple family members from the same family?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And essentially this sample that you selectively picked and interviewed was not a true representative sample of the greater whole of the Kosovo Albanian population. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, let me ask you this: Are you familiar with the concept of a sample group as used in statistics, sociology, medicine and other professional areas of study?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take it then that you have not had any extended formal training or education in that area of study?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of statistics or sociology, I mean I've had a few classes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any persons with formal training in those areas performing the analyses of the interview statements and preparing this report which the Office of the Prosecutor has submitted to us Kosovo/Kosova As Seen, As Told?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have legal training which --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, ma'am. I said did anyone in your staff --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- have training in the area of statistics, sample group methodology, inferential statistical analysis?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had people who were trained lawyers and police officers that had worked on large documentation processes. I couldn't say whether they have this exact experience that you've just rattled. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, if I can ask you. The method that you just described of selecting your sample group, are you aware that it violates the basic tenets of selecting a sample group in order to have a valid and proper inferential and statistical analysis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question. I'm perhaps misunderstanding the situation. But I thought that this was a team of human rights workers out looking for evidence of human rights breaches and not a market research organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps it's because you -- since the report has not yet been examined by the panel, but the report itself goes beyond just reporting what unnamed, unsworn interviewees stated. It goes on to reach conclusions that are applied to a whole and -- far-reaching conclusions that relate to every single refugee and that relate to every single municipality of Kosovo, to reach conclusions based upon what actually happened, et cetera, and I intend to demonstrate the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. What I don't understand is the suggestion that they, that's the monitors carrying this out, selected a sample group as if they were a market research organisation. I don't know the basis of your question is proper in light of the evidence so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the evidence so far has been that the -- at least the claims made by the witness have been that the mission was not biased, that it was impartial, and that it was trying to seek information. What I'm trying to establish is that the manner in which they sought the information was, in fact, of a particular type of bias such that they cannot use the results to try to reach far-reaching conclusions to the entire area of Kosovo and the entire Kosovar population that may have left their homes and for the reasons that they left those homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That may be a perfectly proper submission for you to make in due course, that because of the job they were doing the conclusions that are offered are not appropriate conclusions. All I'm saying to you is that to suggest that they went out of their way to select a sample group as a statistical exercise or something like market research is an improper foundation for the question that you're putting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's not what I was implying. I was trying to question the methodology used to see whether it was suspect or deficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: One thing more which I respectfully prompt him to state. That there are many things which could be inferred from the report itself while we go through the report and could be pointed out at the time of arguments or any other appropriate time. And there's no need of some of the things coming up if they are borne on the report. Thank you for this interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, of course, we still haven't had a ruling whether the report will be admitted into evidence, and there are certain objections to the report, so some of this is necessary, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, ma'am, I take it then that we can conclude that nobody involved in the analysis of the interviews was qualified to prepare an inferential analysis, to apply it to the refugee population as a whole. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is it accurate or is it that there was no such person?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer the question. I don't know the curriculum vitaes of all the people that were involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you offer training --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what you're asking me to do. Not on statistical compilations, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the mission offer training on the concept of simple, random sampling?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you familiar with the concept of a standard deviation or standard of error?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from my old college days. Other than that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does the analysis of your report contain a standard deviation or a standard of error for its analysis and conclusions?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- I don't know. I can't answer that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again. We have to see the report itself and its intrinsic value at that time. Supposing the report is not accepted, then you are saved of the questions. Supposing it is accepted, the report is in a tenable shape and with all these principles which you are very kindly enunciating, it could be with that touch we can always see that. I mean, there would be -- you have all the ample opportunity of your knowledge to be used for that purpose. That is my request.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, since we have deferred ruling on that until the conclusion of the cross-examination of the Defence, unfortunately these are matters that we have discuss now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know or have you had any -- have you read any literature regarding how the size of a sample group affects the validity of inferences drawn therefrom to a population whole?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the recent few years, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was any such literature consulted for the compilation and preparation of this OSCE report that you have been talking about today?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And for the sake of clarity -- you've testified that you have information as to the total population of Kosovo Albanians that lived in the territory of Kosovo Metohija during the time period in question. Is that accurate? You indicated a figure earlier of approximately 1.5, 1.6 million?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said 1.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And based upon that -- based upon that, wouldn't roughly the sample group that you interviewed, 2.764 individuals, wouldn't that roughly account for less than 0.20 of 1 per cent of the Kosovo Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. It was the capacity that we had in the field that led to the number, not the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And as a matter of fact, having read your report, isn't it also accurate that some of the inferences and findings therefrom relating to particular occurrences in particular municipalities are based upon only one interviewee?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where that's the case, it's generally noted in the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But it does exist, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So in that case, your interview of one person led your staff to conclude -- to make a conclusion, a legal conclusion, relating to an entire municipality and an entire occurrence?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was -- there was always additional factors. You'd have to point to the specific reference for me to understand the context, but the municipality reports included also information that we had before leaving Kosovo. So it was more than just one interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe you testified that the training that was received by the various KVM staff was ongoing from November through -- excuse me, through March of 1999. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the period in time in which we were able to do the trainings, but these were not weekly trainings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They were as-needed or as ad hoc maybe?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As needed and as we were able to pull the materials together and prioritise, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, would it be fair to say then yesterday when my colleague Mr. O'Sullivan asked about the adequacy of the training of various staff and certain complaints that had been voiced regarding that adequacy, wouldn't it be fair to say that during the time period when the KVM mission was in Kosovo, that is up until March 1999, insofar as training was still ongoing, it was possible that some of the people in the field were not properly trained?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not properly trained to do what? They were all properly trained to be witnesses, to do documentation, to interview, to record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And -- but they were not properly trained to analyse, were they?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you earlier indicated that no one was trained to perform an analysis of these figures to make an inference with respect to the population whole?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That statement refers to the -- the team in Warsaw that was actually compiling the report. The question I just heard from you was people in the field in Kosovo, the verifiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back for a second to the interviews by your staff in Macedonia and Albania. Isn't it accurate that your report acknowledges that there were inconsistencies between various persons talking about the same occurrence?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Not that there could be, there actually were?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were at times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, I go back to the fact that you earlier stated that everyone told you -- I take that back. You earlier stated that all interviewees told you the same story. Would you care to correct that now at this point in time, now that you've agreed that there were inconsistencies in the statement. Wouldn't it be -- isn't it impossible to have inconsistencies and yet to have everyone be telling you the exact same story as you had earlier testified?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about thousands of crimes. In a particular crime, there may be an inconsistency. In others, like the deportations, there were very -- there were no inconsistencies. So it depends on the crime you're talking about and the situation. There may have been inconsistencies with regards to one actual event.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about your report which acknowledges inconsistencies existing and which you acknowledge was true. So were there inconsistencies in the statements made by interviewees with respect to what's alleged in the 750-page report?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were inconsistencies with regards to a specific event, and where that happened that was noted in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, due to the fact that you lacked personnel, resources, and other factors, isn't it also true that your report acknowledges that was impossible to investigate fully and verify all these instances?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So at the time of the day we're really using a small sample group drawn from a limited pool to reach -- to make far-reaching conclusions that are essentially guesses or that are not verified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down. Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During your tenure at --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think there's a request from the interpreter's booth that counsel slows down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try to. I'm just mindful of the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Mitchell, during your ten years as the head of the human rights department in the KVM operation, and prior to the withdrawal of your mission, I believe you had testified that you had occasion to verify certain criminal activity on the part of the -- on the part of Kosovo Albanian armed groups, particularly the KLA. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, during the time of the KVM mission's tenure in Kosovo Metohija, isn't it true that the KLA conducted numerous attacks against the Serbian police, Serbian civilians, and even Kosovo Albanian civilians that were obstacles to their armed insurgency?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report does document the conduct of the UCK as relates to attacks against police, yes; at times against civilian -- excuse me, Serbian civilians, as well as Kosovo Albanians. That is covered in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it true that the mission verified that the KLA killed not only moderate Albanians who did not support their cause, but also Serbs who were well regarded by both the Serbian and the Albanian communities?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there are reports to that effect, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have statistics for the number of crimes or human rights violations attributed to the UCK, the KLA, during the time period that your mission was in Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Statistics, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Was that not part of the mission objective, to focus on those crimes?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it was. They were documented. I just couldn't rattle off statistics for you, and the information isn't registered in my mind in a statistical way. Of course we documented them. We investigated them when we could, and they're all included in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during that time period are you also familiar with certain publications that came out in the press, in particular in Pristina, Kosovo Albanian newspapers that published lists of Serbs and Albanians that were -- it's kind of like a hit list?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: During what time period?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Up to March of 1999, from the deployment through the departure of the KVM mission.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such reports during that time, but I do afterwards hen the return -- when the refugees came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You don't know whether that was from the time -- whether those were -- papers were actually published prior to your departure -- to the departure or whether they were published after?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just remember seeing those types of newspaper articles that you've described occurring after the end of the conflict, so to speak, and the return of the refugees back into Kosovo. It may have happened beforehand, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall during the time period of the KVM mission being in Kosovo Metohija that there was some incidents of the killings on the part of the KLA which attracted some international attention. For instance, do you recall the killing of six young Kosovo Serb youths in Pec in a bar in December 1998?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Panda Bar, yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you also recall in -- I believe it was that same month, that the deputy mayor of Kosovo Polje, an ethnic Serb, was abducted and murdered by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And regarding abductions and kidnappings which I believe you touched upon in response to some questions from one of my learned colleagues, is it also accurate that your report contains information from the International Committee of the Red Cross stating that as of mid-March 1999, that is when your mission withdrew from Kosovo Metohija, there had been 146 persons of various ethnicities, Serb, Albanian, Romani, Turk, and otherwise, who had been abducted or otherwise unaccounted for in areas controlled by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that number sounds about right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall that your staff -- or I should say the KVM mission, someone from the KVM mission, had meetings with the KLA in December of 1998 to try and determine the fate of persons who had been abducted?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of mission was quite engaged in the issue of the missing, and there were regular discussions to try to obtain information about them from all sources, including the KLA, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall in particular a gentleman by the name of Adem Demaci, D-e-m-a-c-i, and a meeting in December of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Demaci was the spokesperson for the KLA, or political advisor, something like this. And there were meetings with him. I wouldn't be surprised if it happened in December, I just don't remember the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the -- would you -- the report -- your report indicates that at that time Mr. Demaci confirmed that any Serbs abducted during that time ought to be presumed to be dead. Does that fairly reflect the knowledge that KVM had of the activities and the modus operandi of the KLA during the time period you were on the ground over there?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that reflects what Mr. Demaci said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in addition -- in addition to the KLA, weren't there in fact other armed Kosovo Albanian factions operating in various areas of Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, the KLA was not unified in a centrally coordinated way. It had different zone commanders, and so it did tend to look different in different parts of Kosovo. I don't know at times, you know, who was part of the KLA and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in a particular village. Only, you know, that natural village defence groups would form and then they called themselves the KLA. It was difficult to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are you familiar with an organisation called the FARK, the Armed Forces of the Republic of Kosova?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The FARK, that rings -- yes. Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And wasn't it accurate that there was various in-fighting between these various armed Kosovo Albanian groups?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They -- in-fighting, I don't know. I know that they didn't have the same type of organised structure and centralised command. They could behave differently, depending on the zone commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, did you have any information as to the assassination of Ahmet Krasniqi of the FARK who was reported to have been assassinated by the KLA in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at the time that the OSCE-KVM mission was deployed on the ground in Kosovo Metohija, at that time in the beginning wasn't it true that in fact the KLA had been reported to have had ties to terrorist organisations?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the time period just prior to and beginning with your deployment, are you familiar with the so-called October accords, or October agreements between Holbrooke and Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you familiar with the terms of those agreements that were negotiated in October of 1998, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yeah. I never saw the document, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have knowledge of the fact that one of the terms of that agreement was for the Serbian police and the Yugoslav army to scale back their force deployments within the Kosovo Metohija province?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm more familiar with the way that's defined in the agreement between Geremek and Jovanovic, the OSCE and the foreign minister of Yugoslavia, which I think also touched on that. I don't know the details of the Holbrooke agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, have I accurately depicted what the purpose or the goal was leading into the KVM deployment?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal -- one was a cease-fire, and the other was, yes, that there would some scale-back, return to barracks I think was the language that was used. And that there would also be a cease-fire, which both sides violated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, now hold on, ma'am. In the -- in your report, the report indicates that the KLA is the one that repeatedly violated the cease-fire. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did repeatedly violate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In fact, I believe if I can direct your attention to Prosecution Exhibit, I think it's P473.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if the court officer can turn to that exhibit. And if you could turn to the page with the ERN number K0350454. That's -- the ERN page for the page in question is K0350454. It looks like it's page 26 in the text, but I don't know in the scanned version since there was an introduction and table of contents whether it would be the 26th page. That's page -- that's 439. We need 454, so it should be about 16 pages advanced. I've been told that should be page 41 of the exhibit. The page number is again K0350454.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could direct the witness's attention to the beginning of the second-to-last paragraph that begins, and I can -- Ms. Mitchell, does this not say, and I quote: "There were frequent small-scale ambushes against MUP forces by the UCK during the first two and a half months of 1999, clearly breaching any conceptions of a cease-fire"?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would it be a fair to say statement to say then that following the October accords, the KVM observed the activities of the KLA and that the KLA, rather than complying with the cease-fire, re-armed, moved into areas after the Serb forces withdrew, and attacked Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now did the KVM attempt to do anything regarding the KLA's blatant violation of the cease-fire following its deployment?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Were you able to do anything to actually get the KLA to stop attacking Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with any sustainability, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it was a fairly frequent and ongoing problem, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And it was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could speakers please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that there were approximately 1.854 attacks by the KLA during --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, counsel. It's the same thing again which I don't think you're picking up from the interpreters. They're asking for a pause between the questions and the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not getting anything on the headphones, so I will endeavour to slow down. I'm on zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess let me ask the question in a different way. Would it be accurate, ma'am, or do you have a recollection in 1998 that there were approximately 1.854 reported attacks by the KLA against the Serbian forces? Does that sound -- does that sound like in the ballpark?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember every sentence of this report. If that's in the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, from your own personal experiences during the relevant time period, does that range, that numerical range, comport to your recollection of the frequency and the volume of the KLA attacks upon Serbian police/Yugoslavian army units?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say for all of 1998. We were only there for the last few months, and so the number seems a little bit high for me in looking at it from that perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, during the time period that -- the few months in 1998 that the KVM mission was present, were there I would say frequently -- daily attacks by the KLA? How frequent were they?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It would go in waves, you know. You could have a quiet few days, or a quiet week, and then there could be outbreaks suddenly in numerous locations at the same time. I mean, I don't think -- my own recollection was that we never had a cease-fire and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So that would be pretty frequent then?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was pretty frequent. But not -- "daily" is maybe going a bit too far that -- there were days when there wasn't any problems. They were few and far between.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But in any event, frequent enough so that you thought that there was not a cease-fire in place?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now while we're discussing the KLA, would it be fair to say that the KVM personnel noted that the KLA were known to be at times dressed in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be also true to say that the KVM staff concluded in your report that the -- and I quote now: "The vast majority of the rank and file KLA members remained villagers with a weapon."

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also a fact, confirmed by the findings of your staff, that the KLA often was based and formed in villages around a particular family group?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just don't know if it was a family group or, you know, sometimes you would have villages that just weren't all one family. But, yes, they were definitely village-oriented.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Such that it was possible for entire families to perhaps be in -- either recruited or whatever in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And given your knowledge of Kosovo Albanian family structure, would it be fair to say that most families were headed by a patriarch figure?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And getting back to the question we started off with, isn't it true that your report states that again when you went into the refugee camps you sought the assistance of family patriarchs to provide interviewees or witnesses for you?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sought the assistance of community leaders to assist, and some may have been family patriarchs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, community leaders, were there any steps undertaken to ensure that the community leaders contacted were not KLA friendly or KLA --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, absolutely. We were dealing with the humanitarian organisations and the human rights organisations that we had worked with inside Kosovo and established links with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where is that methodology discussed in your report?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report, I believe it's in the section that describes how the information was collected in the camps and that different systems were used in part of Macedonia where you had host families, where many people were living with other Albanians. And so we used a different network in that area, and I think it's in that section of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you can't exclude that perhaps some of the people interviewed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could speakers please make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Ivetic, that that's your third warning, so it's perhaps appropriate for a yellow card to be waved now in the hope that you will observe the pause that's necessary for the interpreter. Bear in mind that you're both speaking the same language, which makes the interpreter's job difficult because the whole of question and answer has to be translated by the one person for those listening on the earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, and now that I can hear the messages on my headphones, I will be mindful of trying to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As I was stating, you cannot exclude the possibility that those persons interviewed may have been referred by KLA members or KLA sympathisers, can you?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, going back to the -- strike that. Going back to the dress practice of the KLA, we had talked about how they often would -- strike that question. We had talked about the fact that KLA members were known to wear civilian clothing. Going further, isn't it a fact that your staff noted or notes in the report that orders -- that it became known that orders had been issued by the KLA leadership, for lack of a better term, to its forces to hide their weapons, shed their uniforms and blend in with civilians when need be?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So, again, based upon that, you cannot exclude that persons that were interviewed may have had affiliations with the KLA in that regard as well?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now it's true, is it not, that the KVM mission -- I guess that's a redundant phrase, but the KVM itself had indications that the KLA was responsible for creating IDPs, and by IDPs I mean internally displaced persons, in Kosovo and Metohija and intentionally using Kosovo Albanian villages as front-line defences in their battles against the Serbian police and the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that in the Kacanik area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And wouldn't it stand to reason that these IDPs could, if they crossed a border, become refugees?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And therefore, ma'am, isn't it also true that you cannot exclude the possibility that some of the 700.000-plus refugees that you did not interview could have left due to this reason, namely the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also a fact that in the report KVM estimates that more than 100.000 Serbian IDPs, again internally displaced persons, had left Kosovo Metohija for Serbia and/or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe that you had testified in the Milosevic case, correct me if I'm wrong, that it was your knowledge that of the few Serbian refugees that you had -- that the organisation had had contact with, these refugees were fleeing exclusively because of the fear from the NATO attacks on Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very few that we were able to interview, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And -- so again, it would stand to reason that we cannot exclude that a portion of the Kosovo Albanian population that left the territory of Kosovo Metohija during that same time period was leaving due to a fear of the NATO attacks that were on place in Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot rule that out, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning for a moment to the NATO attack on Yugoslavia, including Kosovo Metohija, you would agree, would you not, that the attacks by the NATO alliance inflicted considerable damage and loss of life within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considerable -- I can't answer that question. I can answer it with regards to damage that occurred in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not all of Yugoslavia, the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I'm citing to [sic] your report.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So that was limited to Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So there was considerable damage and loss of life within Kosovo Metohija that directly and approximately resulted from the NATO bombing. Is that what your testimony is here today?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was considerable damage. I don't know that we have an exact number on the loss of life, but there was loss of life, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And flowing from that, would it then also be a possible inference that with that situation people would not want to stay around?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A possible inference, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, furthermore, are you aware or did you receive reports of civilians that fled their homes in other parts of Serbia, for instance Belgrade, when NATO attacked Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of it because of the news, not because of any reports that we would have received as part of the field operation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So dealing with those refugees would not have been part of the mandate for your mission?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our -- we were limited to movement in Albania and Macedonia, and many of the Serbians that left would have gone -- stayed within other parts of Serbia and Montenegro and we didn't have access there or a mandate there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you do have general knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in fact, relating back to Kosovo Metohija -- or limiting ourselves to Kosovo Metohija, it's a fact, is it not, that NATO forces struck civilian targets, including convoys of Kosovo Albanians?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have any information as to the intensity of the NATO attacks on the territory of Kosovo Metohija during the time period that the -- you know, that the -- after your mission had left?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- wherever -- whenever a refugee made a reference to NATO bombings or NATO planes, that was noted. And the report does include incidents, the convoy you're talking about. So where it was reported to us by the refugees, it is included in the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry. And in that report there are several such instances that were reported by refugees?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would that not also be a cause for fear among the population of Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any -- yes. Any violence and the use of armed forces is going to create fear, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So again this can be excluded as a cause for why people left their homes?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In fact, I believe your -- the OSCE report acknowledges that there was even a legitimate function of the Serbian police escorting people who were afraid of attacks by either the KLA or NATO aircraft. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's accurate. It's incumbent on security forces to try to protect civilians, and there were some indications in some reports that are also included in the report in this volume 1 of Serbian military and police assisting and helping civilians at times during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And let's focus on some more examples of the specific conduct of the police during the time period. Earlier we had talked about -- strike that. The KVM mission in Kosovo Metohija, it too was fired upon by the KLA and suffered casualties arising therefrom?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember one, one casualty, yes. And cars were getting caught at times in cross-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me see if I can refresh your recollection with some instances. Do you recall an instance sometime in January of 1999 where two KVM personnel were wounded by a sniper on the road near Gornji Ratis, Mr. Martin Feil [phoen] and Dejan Zojaga, and had to be basically sent to the Pristina hospital?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember an incident where there was a shooting and some sort of an injury. It may have been the one you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall at that point in time that the Serbian police came to the assistance of this person -- of these personnel?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would the -- do you also recall that these -- these verifiers had accompanied a police convoy, despite warnings that their safety couldn't be assured?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does sound familiar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe yesterday you mentioned at one point in time that the -- that the Serbian authorities, I don't know if you'd specifically mentioned the police, but they had at times restricted the movement or that you thought that they had restricted the movements of the KVM?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Or that they were uncooperative?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Couldn't another explanation for that be that they were concerned for the safety of the various vehicles and personnel that were being transported?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a case-by-case basis that could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So again we cannot exclude that rationale either?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe there was an instance on January 9th, 1999, in the area of Dasinovac in the Decani municipality where a KVM vehicle containing verifiers was attacked by a rocket-launcher and by small arms and infantry fire. Do you recall that instance?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that one, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk generally then. For any such instance, would it be fair to say that the KVM would have contacted the local Serbian police authorities to ask for assistance?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of any instance where the Serbian police refused to act and refused to offer assistance?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Refused to offer -- sorry. Refused to offer assistance for KVM --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To evacuate --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For KVM staff in distress?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any incidents where the police refused to help in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that the Serbian police were quite cooperative with KVM in that regard?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to extracting people if they got in trouble, it didn't happen very often, fortunately, and when it did there was cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say it didn't happen very often, but it did happen multiple times, did it not?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was there an incident with the Red Cross where a Red Cross vehicle had struck a mine and had been attacked by the KLA and the police came with a helicopter to evacuate the personnel?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you remember the time frame for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe it was in September of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. I do remember it, but we weren't in theatre at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time. Okay.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, isn't it also true that the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs staff in Pristina staff engaged in regular, and I believe it was daily contact, with the KVM?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as part of that daily contact, information was exchanged regarding events that occurred and regarding any actions that had been undertaken by the police against the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at those particular meetings. They were handled by the liaison departments of the mission. But that's my understanding of the general nature of those discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it also your understanding that the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs, that is to say the local police, would advise KVM prior to any actions that they were undertaking against the KLA that were planned?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't have complete knowledge. At times that would happen, but I wouldn't say that it was all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, for instance, in the oft-cited Racak operation, isn't it true that an OSCE-KVM verifier vehicle was present at the scene overlooking the operation from a hilltop, having been previously advised by the police that such an operation was going to be underway?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that's the reason the person was there, but there was verifiers in the area. But I don't know what prompted that particular individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- but you do recall that the vehicle was there overlooking the village of Racak?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that there were verifiers that saw something over hills. I just don't know how much -- the time-frame that they were there, how many hours, et cetera. But, yes, there was reports coming from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, during the time period when your mission was in Kosovo Metohija, wasn't it also true that the Serbian police would cooperate with KVM and notify KVM when they came across any corpses of unidentified dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received notification of dead bodies from the police, yes, as well as from the UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it be fair to say that it would be illogical for the police if they were engaged in killings to give you notice of finding the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not be illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the -- with any instances of misconduct on the part of police officers, when you reported them, isn't it true that corrective measures were applied by the local police?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can I direct your attention to your report -- one moment, please. Again, this is Exhibit P473. The page number is K03504 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've just, I hope, received an e-mail asking you to identify the page number not by this ERN reference but the actual page number of the document. That's the easiest way for it to be located.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It would be, but unfortunately the page number is not the sequential number of the scanned document since the -- the page number I am showing is 49, and I believe on the e-court it's actually not page 49, and I don't know which page it is since I'm looking at a hard copy myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, hold on a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm told it might be page 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That should be the document. And I would direct the witness's attention to the end of that page, and then we'll lead on to the beginning of the next page, and I quote: "In this case the OSCE-KVM discussed with the victims about what they themselves could do and what the OSCE-KVM could do and considered risks involved. They came to the conclusion they should go to the local police in Decani and make a complaint. The OSCE-KVM arranged the meeting and the group met with the police commander, who was the deputy chief of police, on 2 February. The complainants were very nervous, but the deputy chief of police calmed them and acted in a very friendly fashion. He took all necessary notes, he looked at the injuries and the belt that had been used. He became very upset when he had been told about the radio that had been stolen, and he said that that was the worst of it all. He apologised to the complainants and assured them that something like this would not happen again and that he would find and punish the policemen who behaved incorrectly. "On 3 February, the OSCE-KVM met again with the police commander, who assured them that the policemen who had taken the radio had been identified and punished with a reduced salary. The policeman also had to get a new radio, give it to the family and apologise which happened on 3 February. However, the second visit also had the affect that the family once more had to have about 15 policemen on their premises, which they again felt to be very threatening."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, from this description I personally don't see anything that the police, when advised of misconduct, did wrong. Please point me -- point it out to me.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question to me was whether or not the misconduct and corrective action was applied in situations when misconduct was brought to the attention of the authorities. And I would not agree that that was the case all the time, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I did not ask you --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that was the -- that is why I answered as I did. The report speaks for itself. There are reports contained like this to show that the information was collected in an impartial way and there reported. I was thinking of numerous other instances where misconduct was brought to the attention of the authorities and no action was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And ma'am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, would you please find a suitable place to interrupt your cross-examination because we will need to have one more break this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We could take it now, and I could see -- because I would only have probably a few follow-up questions. I can maybe wrap them up and make sure that any questions are few, if any, after the break, and then we can continue with whatever else we need to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at half past 6.00 and sit for just another half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe I have just one or two questions, then I'll be concluding my examination of Ms. Walker -- excuse me, Ms. Mitchell, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to your work for the return of refugees to Kosovo Metohija, are you aware of the fact that the Serbian authorities in 1999 established a Crisis Staff for the return of refugees and established ten centres to assist refugees to return from Macedonia and Albania to Kosovo Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the Kosovo Coordination Centre, the CCK?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was for IDPs, for IDPs, I apologise --

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Centre for IDPs.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In that case, no further questions then.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a clarification. I'm sorry. The -- can you restate the question, because I am aware that there were IDPs in Serbia and that the government was trying to take carry of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is in Kosovo Metohija, ma'am. That there were ten centres established by the Serbian authorities to assist displaced persons to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, okay. No, I don't have that detailed information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You were shown an ICG database form and a comparison was made with the OSCE data form. Just one question on that. Are you aware -- can you comment on how the ICG managed and organised its data? Are you aware?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've been asked to pause before answering. Yes, I am aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And are you aware of how it is managed after it leaves them and it arrives at the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SANDRA MITCHELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That does focus on a point that does concern the Trial Chamber. These two examples that were produced were absolutely identical. There's no room for this being accidental.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And just because of the very detailed nature of the material that's there. And of course the exchange of information in that way is inconsistent with the scheme that the witness has outlined. So I hope that you will either have somebody to explain this later or you will carry out some sort of inquiry to be -- to enable you to explain it to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because it could have an impact, obviously, on the assessment of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think I could explain it. I just asked her that last question to indicate to the Court that she would not be aware as to how these forms that she was shown, the last one, the ICG form was created. So that could explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Will you have evidence to explain it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we need to call a witness to explain how we manage data, raw data, in the OTP storage system, we probably could. But I think it is something that I could indicate to the Court from investigations made -- it's a matter of how raw data is managed in large databases and how they are merged. There are different people bringing in large data. At some point someone is contracted to put it in a database, and sometimes reports from the OSCE might be merged by the ICG with their information. So in other words, the ICG would have information, and at one point they were contracted to work in creating a merged database of many thousands of bits of pieces of raw data that we're getting. And in doing that they merged information from other sources into their own data or database. So you will see an ICG form that has materials identical to another form from another source, because in creating a database there was some merger. That is the explanation I have had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that would presumably be contrary to any protocol you had with them in coming to an agreement with them to handle data when the material that comes from the KVM is - and I'm quoting the witness - highly confidential, therefore you have no right have that or permit the merger of that material, as I understand the position. So are you saying that this is happening deliberately, in contrary -- in contravention of the basis on which the material was provided to you in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or are you saying something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
